items.summary: As LLM capabilities have expanded, multi-agent communication has emerged as an increasingly active area of research. Prevailing protocols often adopt rigid structures that introduce coordination bottlenecks and can degrade as the number of agents increases. We introduce Proxifield, a round-adaptive multi-agent protocol with decentralized agent decision-making that constructs sparse communication graphs from the evolving semantic proximity of agents. Without model training or a centralized planner, Proxifield connects agents using four routing signals derived at inference time: direct address, information needs, plan alignment, and information complementarity. We compare Proxifield with two representative coordination baselines, a centralized Star protocol and a decentralized Shared Context protocol, across two domains: Drone Search and Rescue and the collective-reasoning benchmark HiddenBench. We first ablate base-model capability and find that, in both domains, the performance of Proxifield improves with model size (35B -> 397B parameter model) and Proxifield outperforms all baselines at the largest scale. As team size increases, Proxifield's task-reward advantage over Star widens from 5.4% at (N=5) to 53.0% at (N=25) and 59.5% at (N=50), while Shared Context consistently underperforms both protocols. Proxifield is also substantially more robust to permanent agent failure, retaining 73.6% of its no-failure task reward under the most severe condition, compared with 58.3% for Shared Context and 38.8% for Star. These results demonstrate that decentralized, semantically adaptive routing can improve the scalability and fault tolerance of multi-agent systems.
items.title: Proxifield: Decentralized Multi-Agent Communication through Semantic Proximity

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: This software package contains the code used for the simulation, analysis, and reproducibility of a study on closed-loop digital-twin validation of federated learning updates for methane control in underground mining. The package includes the plant–twin simulator, federated-learning routines, calibration scripts, intervention-budget analyses, attack calibration and backdoor diagnostics, candidate-update generation and scoring, the fresh-seed confirmatory analysis, twin-mismatch sensitivity experiments, exploratory Krum-based comparisons, FLTrust-style diagnostics, serious-harm analyses, and read-only manuscript audits. The evaluation separates the simulated plant used for operational outcome assessment from the imperfect digital twin used for candidate scoring. The repository also documents the distinction between direct plant evaluation and curve-interpolated budget matching used in different experimental stages. Raw methane measurements are not redistributed in this archive. The study uses the public dataset “Methane” by Sikora and Wróbel, available from Mendeley Data, Version 1, DOI: 10.17632/yd7vw4c5mk.1. Instructions for obtaining and preparing the data are provided in DATA.md. The archive includes reproducibility documentation, script-to-manuscript mapping, provenance notes, execution order, software requirements, and SHA-256 checksums. Historical scripts are retained where necessary to document the progression from early exploratory analyses to the final frozen analysis.
items.title: SFDT-DTVRA: Reproducibility Code for Closed-Loop Digital-Twin Validation of Federated

items.summary: This record provides supporting experimental data, source code, selected trained model weights, and reproducibility documentation for the manuscript “RART: A Resource-Aware Recursive Transformer for Stochastic Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling” by Cem Savas Aydin. The study evaluates RART on stochastic resource-constrained project scheduling problems using instances from the Project Scheduling Problem Library (PSPLIB). The primary comparison involves 101 J60 projects, three training seeds per method, and 1,000 common duration scenarios per project. Seven J30 projects provide secondary comparisons. The comparator is an independently trained Wheatley-based graph neural network policy. The uploaded files comprise: ESM_1.pdf: Supplementary methodological documentation, including model features, random streams, evaluation procedures, statistical reconstruction, and provenance. ESM_2.zip: Archived source code, six selected inference checkpoints, project definitions and splits, training records, scenario-level scheduling outcomes, and scripts for reconstructing the reported statistics and figures. Recorded outcomes include mean makespan, upper-tail makespan measured by CVaR90, results before and after schedule repair, and computation times. The README.md file within ESM_2.zip provides instructions for reconstructing the statistical results from the saved simulation outputs without retraining the models.
items.title: Supporting Data and Code for RART: A Resource-Aware Recursive Transformer for Stochastic Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling

items.summary: Empirical reactive force field (RFF) molecular dynamics enables atomistic simulation of bond breaking, bond formation, charge redistribution, and structural evolution in chemically complex systems. The ReaxFF method is arguably the most popular and transferable of the currently available RFF methods. However, routine use of ReaxFF often requires substantial manual effort to prepare inputs, interpret engine-specific outputs, organize simulation artifacts, and develop custom analysis scripts, limiting reproducibility and scalability. Here, we present ReaxKit, a modular Python toolkit for preparing, parsing, analyzing, and managing ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations. ReaxKit uses a separation-of-concerns architecture that distinguishes engine-specific input/output handling, canonical domain data models, scientific analysis, workflow orchestration, presentation, storage, and graphical interaction. Engine adapters convert outputs from supported simulation environments into typed, engine-independent data structures, allowing analysis modules to operate independently of native file formats. User requests are executed through consistent command-line, functional Python, and browser-based graphical interfaces, while a dedicated workspace preserves raw data, normalized datasets, analysis settings, results, logs, caches, and provenance information. Representative applications demonstrate the breadth of the toolkit, including automated generation of elastic and equation-of-state training data from Materials Project structures and mechanical properties, characterization of active sites and local structural environments, and execution of simulation campaigns through YAML-defined study workflows. These capabilities show that ReaxKit supports all essential stages of the ReaxFF workflow.
items.title: ReaxKit: A Modular Python Toolkit for Preparing, Parsing, and Analyzing ReaxFF Molecular Dynamics Simulations

items.summary: Reproducibility release 1.1.0 for Ocean Engineering manuscript OE-D-25-10458. This package supports a controlled Rotterdam-Yokohama comparison of the Suez, Cape and Northern Sea Route corridors using three predefined strategic waypoint philosophies per corridor. The archive contains the Python routing and analysis code, all nine waypoint definitions, frozen maritime-network geometries and scenario/leg distances, dual-coastline quality-assurance and local-repair reports, 0.05/0.025-degree convergence outputs, sourced OpenStreetMap Suez Canal geometry and provenance, downstream time/fuel/CO2 analyses, exponent and vessel-reference sensitivities, and the frozen manuscript sources and figures. The routing method uses searoute 1.4.3, WGS84 distance recomputation and no great-circle fallback. The reproduction command stages the archived routes, regenerates downstream tables and copies the included figure assets. A full routing rerun additionally requires the externally distributed Natural Earth 10 m v5.1.1 and GSHHG 2.3.7 full L1 coastline datasets. Tests and release checks are documented in the archive. The comparison is strategic and does not predict realised voyages or commercial viability.
items.title: Effects of Route Representation on Distance and Downstream Voyage Implications in Europe–Asia Trade: A Comparison of the Suez, Cape, and Northern Sea Route Corridors

items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: Multi-agent active inference gives a natural account of belief sharing: agents hold local posteriors over a shared latent state, communicate those beliefs, and pool them into a colony-level consensus. The same mechanism is fragile when a member is miscalibrated, corrupted, or strategically wrong. Because the standard pool multiplies the reports together, a single confident-but-wrong broadcast that puts near-zero mass on the true state can pull the whole consensus off it, outweighing many honest members. The colony therefore needs a way to preserve the useful structure of belief sharing while limiting the influence of contaminated beliefs. This paper presents Active Fedference, a discrete-categorical framework that connects robust federated generalized variational inference with active inference belief sharing. The main bridge is structural: standard belief sharing appears as the non-robust corner of a broader generalized-Bayes family, while robust losses, conservative server fusion, and explicit aggregation diagnostics describe how the system moves away from that corner under declared contamination mechanisms. The result is not a replacement for belief sharing, but a containment result: ordinary belief sharing is recovered when robustness is turned off. Bounded-loss theory applies on the client axis, while the variational-server axis supplies an objective-backed redescending weight update. Following the manuscript's authoritative three-axis guarantee map, the paper keeps source-conditional client updates, a recovery-only heuristic server rule, and an objective-backed variational server rule as separate claim owners, with no robustness guarantee transferred between them. The study suite then exercises the framework as an end-to-end research system: recovery checks anchor the standard-Bayes limit, belief-sharing studies verify the communication baseline, contamination experiments test robust consensus, and extension studies probe moving agents, hierarchical latent structure, sensitivity to acuity and colony size, parameter recovery, and single-host socket-backed federation traces. All reported quantities are generated from deterministic analysis artifacts and injected into the manuscript by token, so the paper, figures, release package, and validation reports remain tied to the same execution record. The open-source repository is ActiveInferenceInstitute/Active_Fedference. This final-release manuscript uses assigned version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22149133; the bound deposited PDF and repository release are controlled by separate publication gates.
items.title: Robust Belief Sharing in Federated Active Inference: A Recovery-Tested Generalized-Variational Framework for Categorical Contamination-Aware Consensus

items.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems generate collaboration traces that record how agents plan tasks, verify intermediate results, and repair failures. Reusing these procedures requires preserving an action's prerequisites and the outputs needed by subsequent agents. Our empirical studies show that grouping these dependencies into functional memory units improves their retention, while connecting units increases retrieval of the units and links jointly required by a task. The preferred combination of units also changes between instructions and checklists, even when each combination's content is fixed across formats. Updating choices from the outcomes of each combination and format pairing outperforms scoring combinations and formats separately. These findings motivate MACE, a memory-agent co-evolution framework that adapts memory organization and agent memory use through execution feedback. Its MemGoG structure represents functional units as subgraphs of related conditions, actions, and outputs, connecting them through support, conflict, and repair relations. MACE Loop selects task-relevant units and relations within a memory budget and provides each agent with instructions or checklists for its current operation. It records the selected units, presentation formats, agent outputs, and task outcomes to update unit scores and relations for retrieval and inform subsequent presentation choices. Across eight benchmarks, MACE outperforms ten baselines with an average score of 81.11%, compared with 78.97% for the strongest baseline, SAGE.
items.title: MACE: Memory-Agent Co-Evolution with Adaptive Memory Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
items.title: When gravity adds useful information to interpretation-conditioned post-stack seismic inversion: reproducibility archive

items.summary: Long-term memory is essential for large language model (LLM) agents to maintain consistency and personalization over extended interactions. Existing memory systems typically rely on fixed granularities or static schemas, but these designs struggle when heterogeneous information, such as preferences, events, constraints, and temporal updates, is embedded in a single mixed representation. The resulting semantic interference makes top-K retrieval sensitive to noise and often leaves relevant evidence poorly ranked. We present AutoViewMem, a data-driven framework that organizes long-term conversational memory into self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views before indexing. AutoViewMem discovers candidate views from interaction traces, selects a compact complementary view set, and uses these views to guide write-time structured extraction of provenance-grounded memories. This representation-first design moves semantic disentanglement from retrieval time to write time, allowing standard top-K similarity search to retrieve focused evidence without explicit routing or iterative retrieval. We further apply offline consolidation to improve memory compactness and consistency. Experiments on the LoCoMo and PersonaMem benchmarks, under both Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B backbones, show that AutoViewMem improves long-horizon question answering and personalization over strong memory baselines while preserving a simple inference pipeline.
items.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory

items.summary: PLANETS SSbD Training on EcoTrace Tool for Digital Product Passports This data entry contains training materials for the EcoTrace Tool and its employment for DPP. It includes: (1) video clip on the intro, bbackground, aiming of DPP in PLANETS, data model of EcoTrace, its connection to SSbD methodology, first testing feedback. (2) a slide set on the topics covered in the video clip, (3) a txt-version as Readme file for the summary of the EcoTrace trraining session. in short: Major take-aways DPP is intended to be a key mechanism for operationalising and communicating SSbD information across product value chains. FAIR data principles are fundamental to DPP implementation , particularly interoperability, machine readability, metadata, identifiers, provenance and controlled accessibility. PLANETS aims to connect the SSbD assessment workflow with DPP data , including information generated across the different assessment tiers and dimensions. EchoTrace is being developed as a flexible, sector-agnostic DPP management tool , allowing customised data models, product types, field groups and user permissions. Different stakeholders require different levels of access ; confidentiality and controlled access are therefore central considerations rather than all DPP information being universally public. Blockchain and Hyperledger Fabric are being explored to support traceability and data integrity , with transactions governed through authorised operations and smart contracts. The practical exercises identified usability and implementation issues , particularly around field groups, permissions, product status, data integrity and how different stakeholders contribute to the same product passport. Industry willingness to provide information is a significant consideration , especially where data involve intellectual property, confidentiality or commercially sensitive information. Future development will focus on standardisation, semantic/metadata dictionaries, blockchain integration and potential EU registry integration. The successful implementation of DPPs will depend not only on technology but also on governance, data granularity, confidentiality, interoperability and stakeholder trust.
items.title: PLANETS SSbD Training on EcoTrace Tool for DPP

items.summary: This record contains the experimental reproducibility package accompanying the study “Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering.” The package provides the complete Jupyter notebook, generated figures, run-level results, aggregated summaries, parameter-sensitivity analyses, bootstrap-stability estimates, drift-response measurements, and paired statistical comparisons. The experimental evaluation compares Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), Possibilistic C-Means (PCM), Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM), and entropy-regularized FCM across five datasets: Iris, Wine, Breast Cancer Wisconsin, Digits represented by four unsupervised principal components, and an imbalanced overlapping synthetic dataset. The methods are evaluated under baseline conditions, Gaussian measurement noise, missing values followed by median imputation, and partial mean-shift drift. The full protocol uses ten paired random seeds, three initializations per fit, and twenty bootstrap resamples for each dataset–scenario–model combination. Class labels are excluded from model fitting and hyperparameter selection and are used only for external evaluation. The archive is organised into code, figures, and results directories. The notebook contains the complete workflow required to reproduce the reported experiments.
items.title: Experimental Reproducibility Package for "Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering"

items.summary: Solver, driver scripts and every numerical output of a study of the efficiency and the retrieved-mode noise of a Lambda-type atomic quantum memory. The model is the one-dimensional Maxwell-Bloch system of a three-level ensemble with the anti-Stokes four-wave-mixing channel, integrated in JAX/Diffrax so that the derivative of an observable with respect to the control field comes from a reverse pass through the propagation. The noise observable is one row of the Bogoliubov kernel projected on the retrieved temporal mode, obtained without assembling the kernel. The outputs cover: the efficiency-noise front traced over a 32-knot control at two signal detunings; the largest singular value of the storage-retrieval map along that front and its dependence on the four-wave-mixing coupling; the spin-wave growth of the resonant anti-Stokes configuration over 2.5 decades of optical depth and a factor 15 in control amplitude; the efficiency, noise photon number and collinear phase mismatch of a cesium configuration taken from published experimental parameters; the derivative of each front point with respect to the optical depth, the spin decoherence, the phase mismatch and the four-wave-mixing coupling, each from one reverse pass; three optimizers compared at one evaluation budget and at three control dimensions, with the cost of a gradient measured against the cost of an objective on the same working point; the number of temporal modes the storage map resolves, on a ladder in the basis size at two spatial grids; the Doppler-averaged absorption of a warm vapour in closed form; three velocity quadratures measured against that closed form and against its derivative, which is the average the field's source carries; the integrator step a velocity-resolved solve needs, which is not the step the front was traced at; the landed controls of the second detuning read again under a 300 K Maxwellian, at one velocity class and at thirty; the Bogoliubov identity projected on the retrieved mode, evaluated at every front point; the noise the detector gate collects over every temporal mode, by stochastic trace estimation, and the effective mode count it gives against the retrieved-mode count; the same trace against the gate's own length; a manifest of every landed run with its detuning, step specification, bound and outcome; the reproducibility of the front, measured as the disagreement between two runs of one control that reach the same efficiency, and what that reproducibility does to a slope read off the front; and the front re-traced at a constant integrator step over both searches, with the local logarithmic slope read on it at three efficiencies fixed before the set was read.  Every output file is plain text carrying its own configuration in a header and a machine-readable RESULT line; DEPOSIT.md maps the directories and names the script that produces each. The archive is a git archive of one commit, so the tree is exactly what that revision held.
items.title: Simulation outputs for a differentiable Maxwell-Bloch model of a Lambda-type atomic quantum memory with four-wave mixing

items.summary: Description : Classeur canonique source-par-source (66 feuilles) sous-tendant l'article "Data-Audited Elastic, Hardness, and Heterostructure-Compatibility Assessment of MAX Phases and MXenes". Contient : l'audit élastique et de dureté des 44 phases MAX canoniques et 11 MXenes ; l'audit de provenance des paramètres de maille ; la matrice de compatibilité dataset-pair des hétérostructures MAX/MAX (461 combinaisons admissibles) ; le screening de durcissement par contraste élastique validé contre des superréseaux expérimentaux (Fiantok et al. 2023) ; les propriétés d'interface (module biaxial, énergie de cohérence) ; la contrainte thermique de désaccord ; et la synthèse applicative orientée revêtements de protection. Chaque feuille documente sa source primaire (DOI), son statut de preuve (EXPERIMENTAL/DFT/UNKNOWN explicite), et une feuille de validation trace les vérifications de non-régression appliquées à chaque étape. Tableaux supplémentaires S1 (tenseur élastique et modules dérivés des 44 phases MAX canoniques), S2 (constantes élastiques 2D et E2D dérivé de 11 systèmes MXene), S3 (valeurs de dureté expérimentales avec charge, méthode, état d'échantillon et niveau de preuve). items.summary: Graph-enhanced multi-agent systems (G-MAS) coordinate large language model agents through communication graphs and role assignments, which determine how agents exchange information and divide responsibilities. However, final-score comparisons across systems combine differences in models, communication patterns, roles, and computation costs, making performance differences difficult to attribute to specific communication structures, role assignments, and information flows. To address this evaluation attribution problem, we introduce OpenMAS-GCom, a benchmark for diagnosing how these components affect G-MAS performance through controlled interventions. We represent systems through collaboration units, communication links, shared intermediate information, and execution rules. OpenMAS-GCom compares original systems with versions modified by changing one component while keeping tasks, models, prompts, and budget limits fixed. We rewire communication edges, remove specialist or critic agents, replace intermediate messages with incorrect content, and disable workers during execution. The benchmark evaluates 17 single-agent, ordinary multi-agent, and graph-enhanced configurations on 29 datasets across six domains. We add 400 G-MAS-Complex tasks requiring agents to combine information from multiple documents, resolve conflicting records, and return specified values with source identifiers. Experiments show larger mean losses after specialist removal than after critic removal, different performance degradation under incorrect messages and worker failures despite similar original scores, and different configurations achieving the highest accuracy and accuracy per token on G-MAS-Complex.
items.title: OpenMAS-GCom. A Diagnostic Benchmark for Graph-enhanced Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: This record contains replication materials for “AI-intensive scientific collaboration exposes unequal coverage in name-based bibliometrics” by Anirban Adhikary and Sourav Bikash Borah. The archive contains the public analysis code, environment specifications, documentation, public-safe aggregate materials, frozen reference outputs, figure sources, and verification tools associated with the study. The public archive reproduces and verifies results within the documented derived-input boundary. It does not redistribute the approximately 770 GB OpenAlex source snapshot. Certain author-level derived inputs, including identifier-bearing bibliometric, name, affiliation, and network records, are excluded from public release because their combination creates a material reidentification risk. Full controlled reproduction requiring these inputs is available subject to an approved research purpose, identity verification, appropriate data-use conditions, and applicable third-party restrictions. The archive documents the analytical workflow, software environment, input contracts, cryptographic hashes, output lineage, and the distinction between public verification and controlled-input execution. The reported analyses are associational.
items.title: Replication package for "AI-intensive scientific collaboration exposes unequal coverage in name-based bibliometrics"

items.summary: Discovering the structure and kinetics of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) from time-series concentration data is a fundamental challenge in chemical kinetics, with existing approaches relying on prior mechanistic assumptions or suffering from high computational cost and noise sensitivity. In this work, we present integral chemical reaction neural networks (iCRNNs), a framework that combines the interpretable, physics-constrained, architecture of chemical reaction neural networks (CRNNs) with an integral collocation formulation of the governing dynamics. Rather than solving ODEs forward in time at each training step, we approximate the integral of the learned rate functions directly using numerical quadrature. This yields an entirely algebraic forward pass consisting only of matrix operations, eliminating the repeated adaptive ODE solves of standard CRNN and producing smoother, more predictable training. We provide a recovery error analysis characterising the structural sources of ill-conditioning (conservation laws, reaction reversibility, and shared reactant sets) that limit network identifiability. On two benchmark CRNs, iCRNN trains in roughly half the wall-clock time of the baseline CRNN method on a four-species mechanism and between three and four times faster on a five-species mechanism, while completing every training run reliably and attaining comparable or lower loss.
items.title: Integral chemical reaction neural networks

items.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems generate collaboration traces that record how agents plan tasks, verify intermediate results, and repair failures. Reusing these procedures requires preserving an action's prerequisites and the outputs needed by subsequent agents. Our empirical studies show that grouping these dependencies into functional memory units improves their retention, while connecting units increases retrieval of the units and links jointly required by a task. The preferred combination of units also changes between instructions and checklists, even when each combination's content is fixed across formats. Updating choices from the outcomes of each combination and format pairing outperforms scoring combinations and formats separately. These findings motivate MACE, a memory-agent co-evolution framework that adapts memory organization and agent memory use through execution feedback. Its MemGoG structure represents functional units as subgraphs of related conditions, actions, and outputs, connecting them through support, conflict, and repair relations. MACE Loop selects task-relevant units and relations within a memory budget and provides each agent with instructions or checklists for its current operation. It records the selected units, presentation formats, agent outputs, and task outcomes to update unit scores and relations for retrieval and inform subsequent presentation choices. Across eight benchmarks, MACE outperforms ten baselines with an average score of 81.11%, compared with 78.97% for the strongest baseline, SAGE.
items.title: MACE: Memory-Agent Co-Evolution with Adaptive Memory Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Code and data to reproduce all analyses and the figure in O'Dea et al. (2026) "Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports". Includes Python scripts for the reef-logger upwelling indices, the bay-wide composite index, the observer set records, the anchoveta length and weight series, the unified 1956 to 2025 landings series, and the main figure together with every statistic reported in the paper. Data include weekly sonde casts from the three deep central stations of the Bay of Panama, continuous reef temperature loggers from the Gulf of Panama running since 1995, the Copernicus Marine Service biogeochemical reanalysis of net primary production (1994 to 2026), anchoveta and thread herring landings spliced from the digitised national stock assessment (1956 to 2014) and the ARAP landings register (2015 to 2025, 332,610 records across 206 taxa), 3,077 onboard observer purse-seine set records (2017 to 2025), 645 dockside proximate assays of landed anchoveta (2016 to 2025), and fish oil and fishmeal export tabulations from INEC customs statistics (1997 to 2025). The archive is self-contained and rebuilds the figure and all reported statistics from the raw sources whenever the derived and figures directories are deleted. Instructions for use, including execution order, software dependencies, directory structure, the provenance of every source and the known caveats, are in README.md. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 and code under the MIT Licence.
items.title: Code and data for: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports

items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models built on pretrained vision-language models have demonstrated strong performance across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. However, VLA models that directly map current 2D observations to actions often lack sufficient spatial and temporal understanding, limiting their performance in precise and long-horizon manipulation. Recent methods enhance VLA models through geometric supervision and future-state prediction across the entire scene. However, these methods can suffer from redundant scene information, distracting the model from learning the geometry and dynamics relevant to the current interaction. To address this issue, we propose FOCAL-VLA, a framework that combines subtask-guided geometry distillation with implicit world modeling to learn representations of current spatial structure and future interaction dynamics. To focus geometric learning on the current subtask, we transfer geometric knowledge from VGGT to the VLA model by aligning geometry latents with features from subtask-relevant image regions. To capture the future 3D evolution of the current interaction, we incorporate implicit world modeling using Track4World features from current and future demonstration frames. The two complementary representations jointly guide action generation without running VGGT or Track4World at inference time. Experiments show that FOCAL-VLA outperforms baselines on both simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks. Project website: https://zhiyuan-gao.github.io/FOCAL-VLA/.
items.title: FOCAL-VLA: Subtask-Guided Geometry Distillation and Implicit World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

items.summary: This release contains the SMT-LIB2 benchmarks accompanying our paper, "Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown." It includes 16 benchmarks covering load-store queue sizes of 8, 16, 32, and 64 entries. Each size includes a secure baseline and three MPX Trojan variants: Base, Bound, and Illegal Memory Access. A verification script runs the benchmarks using Z3, checks the results against the expected outcomes, and saves the solver output and execution times.
items.title: Supporting Code for Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown

items.summary: As LLM capabilities have expanded, multi-agent communication has emerged as an increasingly active area of research. Prevailing protocols often adopt rigid structures that introduce coordination bottlenecks and can degrade as the number of agents increases. We introduce Proxifield, a round-adaptive multi-agent protocol with decentralized agent decision-making that constructs sparse communication graphs from the evolving semantic proximity of agents. Without model training or a centralized planner, Proxifield connects agents using four routing signals derived at inference time: direct address, information needs, plan alignment, and information complementarity. We compare Proxifield with two representative coordination baselines, a centralized Star protocol and a decentralized Shared Context protocol, across two domains: Drone Search and Rescue and the collective-reasoning benchmark HiddenBench. We first ablate base-model capability and find that, in both domains, the performance of Proxifield improves with model size (35B -> 397B parameter model) and Proxifield outperforms all baselines at the largest scale. As team size increases, Proxifield's task-reward advantage over Star widens from 5.4% at (N=5) to 53.0% at (N=25) and 59.5% at (N=50), while Shared Context consistently underperforms both protocols. Proxifield is also substantially more robust to permanent agent failure, retaining 73.6% of its no-failure task reward under the most severe condition, compared with 58.3% for Shared Context and 38.8% for Star. These results demonstrate that decentralized, semantically adaptive routing can improve the scalability and fault tolerance of multi-agent systems.
items.title: Proxifield: Decentralized Multi-Agent Communication through Semantic Proximity

items.summary: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are highly sensitive to label noise, since corrupted supervision can propagate through the graph and degrade learned node representations. This work proposes PCC+GCN, a hybrid framework that uses Particle Competition and Cooperation (PCC) as a graph-based label-refinement stage before GCN training. PCC identifies suspicious labeled nodes through particle domination dynamics and determines whether their labels should be preserved, removed, or reassigned before GCN training. The framework also allows the graph used by PCC to be augmented with feature-based $k$-nearest-neighbor edges, while the GCN itself is trained on the original graph structure and node features. The proposed method was evaluated on ten graph datasets from the NoisyGL benchmark under conventional Uniform, Pair, and Random label noise, as well as under instance-dependent label noise. A detailed hyperparameter analysis was also conducted on Cora, CiteSeer, and PubMed. Under conventional noise, PCC+GCN achieved the highest overall average accuracy and the best average rank among the evaluated methods, with an average gain of $1.67$ percentage points over the baseline GCN across the clean setting and all noisy scenarios. Under instance-dependent noise, PCC+GCN remained competitive with the best-performing robust methods while requiring substantially lower execution time, being the fastest robust method on eight of the ten datasets. The results indicate that PCC-based label refinement provides an effective and computationally efficient preprocessing strategy for improving GCN robustness under noisy supervision.
items.title: Particle Competition and Cooperation for Robust Graph Convolutional Network Learning Under Label Noise

items.summary: Large language models have shown strong potential as role-playing agents for real individuals, yet faithful impersonating remains challenging. Existing in-context learning-based methods fail to capture how individuals react under different situations. In addition, LLM-based evaluation is difficult for obscure individuals. To address these challenges, we propose Situation--Internal state--Behavior Persona method to incorporate situation-dependent behavioral strategies. We further design an evaluation protocol that provides LLM evaluators with references about the impersonated individual. We evaluate our approach on a newly constructed dataset for the task of generating replies on social media. Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art ICL-based baselines, while our evaluation protocol achieves moderate correlation with human judgment. Besides, experiments on fictional-character benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed method is applicable beyond the social media setting. These findings suggest that incorporating behavioral information broadly improves the fidelity of role-playing for real individuals on social media or fictional characters.
items.title: From Memory to Behavior: A Behavior-Aware Role-Playing Framework for Social Media Influencers

items.summary: Ransomware increasingly fragments its file operations across temporary and intermediate files, scattering the semantic context that links individual I/O events to an overarching encryption campaign. This fragmentation defeats existing detectors that reason over isolated file streams -- whether pattern-based methods that match rigid event sequences or learning-based methods that require accumulating statistical evidence across many files. We present DEFEAT, a framework that reconstructs this fragmented, scattered context by grouping causally related file events into File Event Gadgets (FEGs), semantically coherent units that capture the full intent behind sequences of file operations spanning multiple dynamically created files. Unlike provenance graphs (system-wide causal graphs that record relationships among all OS entities, such as processes, files, sockets, and registry keys, across the entire system), FEGs are scoped to the file-operation context of a single user asset, enabling lightweight, targeted analysis without whole-system instrumentation. Each FEG is modelled as an attributed control flow graph (ACFG) and embedded via a graph neural network for unsupervised clustering, enabling analysts to label entire behavioural clusters rather than individual samples, reducing annotation effort by 94%. Evaluated on a corpus of 97,816,471 file I/O events spanning 67 ransomware families, DEFEAT achieves 99.2% detection accuracy and outperforms state-of-the-art methods including UNVEIL, RWGuard, and Peeler by 6.57 to 7.56%. The framework operates at the granularity of a single file encryption: because each ACFG represents exactly one FEG (one user asset context), a cluster label can be assigned as soon as the first file operation completes, enabling detection at the first encrypted file.
items.title: DEFEAT: Stitching Fragmented File I/O Contexts for Early Ransomware Detection

items.summary: Abstract Modern enterprise AI systems increasingly operate across multiple authorized data sources, memories, applications, and tools. This creates a security problem that is not adequately described as conventional data theft. An AI workload may be individually authorized to read support records, engineering information, source-control activity, supplier data, budgets, hiring information, and calendars. No individual source may contain a sensitive strategic conclusion. However, the AI system may combine those independently authorized fragments and reconstruct a new high-value object: an unreleased product direction, likely launch window, supplier dependency, market strategy, organizational weakness, or other forward-looking enterprise knowledge. The security boundary therefore changes. The relevant questions are no longer only: Who may read data A? or: Who may read data B? They also become: Who may establish the relationship A-to-B? Who may retain or disclose the resulting inference? Who may cause an external action because of that reconstructed meaning? This paper describes a threat model in which the AI assistant becomes a computational graph across previously separate enterprise systems. The resulting risk may exist even when each underlying retrieval complies with its ordinary source-level permissions. The sensitive object is not necessarily a stolen database record; it may be a new semantic object created through authorized association. The architecture therefore separates two security transitions: Authorized Data | v Authorized Reconstruction | v Computed Meaning | v Authorized Effectuation | v External Consequence The first transition concerns association authority : permission to read independently authorized fragments does not automatically imply permission to join those fragments into a new semantic relationship. The second concerns execution-time finality : permission to compute, generate, or prepare an output does not automatically imply permission for that output to become externally consequential. The proposed architectural model therefore introduces controls around independently governed relationship mapping, session-bound reconstruction, minimum-necessary temporary views, provenance-aware release, and a mandatory effectuation boundary. Candidate outputs or actions remain non-effective until the consequence-controlling component verifies the applicable authority, provenance, destination, policy state, disclosure conditions, and other protected execution state immediately before release or effectuation. In compact form: Access != Association Association != Authority to Disclose Computation != Authority to Cause Consequence The execution-time consequence boundary may be implemented through existing mechanisms such as policy-enforcement points, reference monitors, authorization servers, secure execution environments, transaction coordinators, capability systems, protected dispatchers, database commit controls, network command gates, or equivalent mechanisms. The important property is functional rather than terminological: A computed result or proposed action remains non-effective until the component with mandatory control over the actual consequence verifies that the exact pending effect is permitted under current protected authority and state. This architecture is intended to complement conventional identity, access control, encryption, zero-trust, data-loss prevention, confidential-computing, logging, and authorization systems rather than replace them. Those mechanisms continue to protect identities, stores, channels, and individual permissions. The additional problem addressed here is governance of the relationship created between authorized fragments and governance of the transition from computed meaning to actual consequence . The paper presents this as a forward-looking threat model rather than an allegation concerning any specific enterprise or AI product. The objective is to identify an architectural risk
items.title: Enterprise AI as a Reconstruction Layer: Governing Derived Knowledge and Execution-Time Consequences

items.summary: Clustering is a fundamental task in data analysis, typically addressed through centroid-based methods such as K-means. In this work, we present a general framework for multi-domain clustering via measure quantization: given samples from multiple domains, we learn a shared set of cluster prototypes by minimizing a probability metric, such as the Sinkhorn divergence or the Maximum Mean Discrepancy, between each domain's probability measure and the measure of prototypes. Data points are then assigned to clusters either via nearest centroid, or via optimal transport, a collaborative strategy that couples all samples within a domain. A mini-batch optimization strategy makes both fitting and assignment scalable, reducing memory and computational cost while preserving clustering performance. Experimental results on 5 multi-domain benchmarks spanning image, audio and sensor data show that our Sinkhorn-based method consistently outperforms classical and multi-domain clustering baselines, and that this advantage persists when scaling to hundreds of thousands of samples.
items.title: Multi-Domain Clustering via Measure Quantization

items.summary: A medical model's benchmark score does not establish that the same conclusion holds under a different evaluation. This study tests whether claims about model ranking, score reliability and screening performance survive changes in cohort, prompt, negative spectrum, specified prevalence and operating threshold. We audit three medical vision-language models (BioMedCLIP, CheXficient, and MedSigLIP) and a general-domain OpenCLIP comparator on 12,200 chest radiograph records from four datasets (Montgomery, Shenzhen, TBX11K, and VinDr-CXR). Five fixed prompt families yield 244,000 model--image--prompt scores. No model leads every cohort and reliability criterion. Prompt-family changes alter AUROC in 21 of 48 multiplicity-controlled comparisons. Replacing healthy controls with sick non-tuberculosis controls reduces AUROC by 0.075--0.306 across all four models. On VinDr-CXR, the three medical models distinguish tuberculosis from no-finding controls substantially better than from pneumonia or lung tumor; their AUROC point estimates for both named diseases fall below 0.5. CheXficient has documented VinDr-CXR pretraining exposure, which limits the interpretation of its results. Thresholds chosen for 95\% sensitivity on TBX11K training retain that constraint by point estimate in only four of sixteen target evaluations. A five-seed supervised source model reaches 0.999 AUROC on TBX11K validation but 0.629 on each of two external cohorts. Conservative exclusion of perceptual-overlap candidates narrows this gap without closing it. These retrospective, single-task results show that discrimination, score reliability and threshold retention support different portability claims. Evidence for chest X-ray tuberculosis screening should identify the complete evaluation specification rather than attribute clinical portability to a checkpoint alone.
items.title: Beyond Benchmark Scores: Auditing Medical Vision-Language Models for Chest X-Ray Tuberculosis Screening

items.summary: Supporting material for the manuscript "Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus): a threshold-anchored dose-response study of steroidogenesis, sperm quality, redox balance and spermatogenic histopathology" (Elbeeh, Filfilan, Filfilan and Filfilan), submitted to Drug and Chemical Toxicology (Taylor & Francis). Forty adult male Swiss albino (ICR) mice, 8-10 weeks old and 22.1-25.5 g at allocation, received vehicle (distilled water) or technical-grade glyphosate at 10, 50 or 100 mg/kg/day by oral gavage for 28 days, n = 10 per group. The dose range brackets the regulatory no-observed-adverse-effect level of approximately 50 mg/kg/day. Endpoints measured in the same 40 animals: body and testis weight; serum testosterone, LH and FSH; epididymal sperm concentration, progressive motility, viability and morphology; testicular malondialdehyde, reduced glutathione, superoxide dismutase and catalase; and testis histopathology stained with haematoxylin-eosin and with periodic acid-Schiff, assessed by the Johnsen tubular-maturation score and by measurement of seminiferous tubule diameter, germinal epithelial height and graded lesion severity. Sections were digitised on a Philips UltraFast Scanner at the x20 level (0.5 micrometres per pixel) and reviewed in the Philips PathologySuite viewer; morphometry was performed in ImageJ v1.54 with semi-automated annotation in QuPath v0.4.3 on fields exported at the native scan resolution. Contents: S1, the manufacturer's Certificate of Analysis for the test article (Sigma-Aldrich 337757, lot MKCZ1523, purity at least 96 per cent, CAS 1071-83-6); S2, analytical kits, instruments, assay conditions and intra- and inter-assay coefficients of variation; S3, the analysis and figure-plotting code; S4, the complete per-animal dataset underlying every figure and table; S5, the benchmark-dose model set with BMD and BMDL10 values; Supplementary Figure S6 with its caption, showing the histomorphometry and graded lesion scores of Table 4 with individual animal values overlaid; S7, the completed ARRIVE 2.0 checklist; S8, the full statistical record for all 30 endpoints (Shapiro-Wilk and Levene checks, the test applied, post-hoc comparisons, effect sizes, Benjamini-Hochberg q values, Jonckheere-Terpstra trend statistics, dose-response correlations and benchmark-dose fits) together with the group mean, SEM and n behind every plotted point; and S9, the unmodified field exported from the whole-slide image behind each panel of Figures 4 and 5, both plates before the arrows were drawn, a manifest of exactly what was done to each image, and checksums. README.md gives the full manifest. Every value reported in the manuscript can be recomputed from S4 using the code in S3. Statistics: continuous endpoints were compared by Welch's ANOVA with the Games-Howell post-hoc test; ordinal lesion grades by the Kruskal-Wallis test with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc test; monotonic trend by the Jonckheere-Terpstra test; and the endpoint family was controlled at a false-discovery rate of 5 per cent (Benjamini-Hochberg). The Johnsen tubular-maturation score was nominated in advance as the primary endpoint; every other endpoint is secondary. Ethics: all procedures were approved by the Bioethics Committee of Umm Al-Qura University, Makkah, Saudi Arabia (approval no. HAPO-02-K-012-2025-04-2781) and were conducted in accordance with the ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines. These 40 animals also support the cardiotoxicity, neurotoxicity and immunotoxicity arms of the same programme, which are reported separately under the same approval number. Licensed CC BY 4.0. Version 2.0.0 adds S8 and S9, replaces S3 with a copy that also carries requirements.txt, a README and the benchmark-dose output table, and replaces the Supplementary Figure S6 image with a copy from which a non-standard private PNG chunk, added in transit and carrying no image information, has been removed. No reported value changed between versions 1.
items.title: Supplementary data and analysis code for: Subacute oral glyphosate impairs testicular function in male mice (Mus musculus)

README.md gives the full manifest. Every value reported in the manuscript can be recomputed from S4 using the code in S3. Statistics: continuous endpoints were compared by Welch's ANOVA with the Games-Howell post-hoc test; ordinal lesion grades by the Kruskal-Wallis test with Holm-adjusted Dunn's post-hoc test; monotonic trend by the Jonckheere-Terpstra test; and the endpoint family was controlled at a false-discovery rate of 5 per cent (Benjamini-Hochberg). The Johnsen tubular-maturation score was nominated in advance as the primary endpoint; every other endpoint is secondary. Ethics: all procedures were approved by the Bioethics Committee of Umm Al-Qura University, Makkah, Saudi Arabia (approval no. HAPO-02-K-012-2025-04-2781) and were conducted in accordance with the ARRIVE 2.0 guidelines. These 40 animals also support the cardiotoxicity, neurotoxicity and immunotoxicity arms of the same programme, which are reported separately under the same approval number. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

items.summary: Traditional unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods are designed to flag or localise deviations from a normative distribution, ignoring the underlying generative mechanisms of the anomalies. Yet the nature of an anomaly is often as important as its presence. We reformulate UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem, in which the objective is to infer the most probable corruption responsible for each observation. Our framework yields a probabilistic anomaly score as the energy of the inferred corruption parameters, and serves as a principled recipe for developing new UAD algorithms. We derive several existing methods as instances of the general framework, each corresponding to the same energy score under different modelling choices. Experimentally, we study the framework's components in a controlled setting, and improve object-class AUROC on the MVTec AD dataset by 2.3% by adapting the underlying corruption model. Finally, we validate the framework on a brain MRI benchmark, achieving strong detection performance while producing estimates of pathology intensity, bias, and geometry. Code is available at https://github.com/jgmyles/inverse-uad.
items.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

items.summary: The article substantiates the importance of ecological education as a pedagogical means of forming a healthy lifestyle among young people and presents the results of a pedagogical experiment. An integrated 36-hour “Eco-Health” module was developed that links environmental topics (air quality, safe water, food systems, active mobility and green spaces, waste and chemicals, climate and heat) with personal health practices, and uses local data, field practicums, self-monitoring and group projects. The quasi-experimental study with pre-test and post-test measurements involved 130 first- and second-year students of a pedagogical higher education institution (experimental group n = 66; control group n = 64) during one semester. After the intervention, the experimental group showed significant improvements in eco-health knowledge (from 46.9 to 65.6 points), attitudes, pro-environmental behaviour and the healthy-lifestyle index (HPLP-II: 2.47 → 2.67), while changes in the control group were minimal; the between-group differences remained significant after adjustment for baseline values (ANCOVA, p < 0.01 for all outcomes). Weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in the experimental group increased by 32 minutes, and the share of students meeting the WHO recommendation rose from 34.8% to 62.1%. The results show that ecological education built on action competence, local relevance and the co-benefits of environmental and health behaviour is an effective tool for forming a healthy lifestyle and can be integrated into the system of continuous education in Uzbekistan.
tags: ecological education; environmental education; healthy lifestyle; health promotion; students; pedagogical experiment; action competence; physical activity; Uzbekistan.
items.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF ECOLOGICAL EDUCATION IN FORMING A HEALTHY LIFESTYLE

items.summary: Multi-agent active inference gives a natural account of belief sharing: agents hold local posteriors over a shared latent state, communicate those beliefs, and pool them into a colony-level consensus. The same mechanism is fragile when a member is miscalibrated, corrupted, or strategically wrong. Because the standard pool multiplies the reports together, a single confident-but-wrong broadcast that puts near-zero mass on the true state can pull the whole consensus off it, outweighing many honest members. The colony therefore needs a way to preserve the useful structure of belief sharing while limiting the influence of contaminated beliefs. This paper presents Active Fedference, a discrete-categorical framework that connects robust federated generalized variational inference with active inference belief sharing. The main bridge is structural: standard belief sharing appears as the non-robust corner of a broader generalized-Bayes family, while robust losses, conservative server fusion, and explicit aggregation diagnostics describe how the system moves away from that corner under declared contamination mechanisms. The result is not a replacement for belief sharing, but a containment result: ordinary belief sharing is recovered when robustness is turned off. Bounded-loss theory applies on the client axis, while the variational-server axis supplies an objective-backed redescending weight update. Following the manuscript's authoritative three-axis guarantee map, the paper keeps source-conditional client updates, a recovery-only heuristic server rule, and an objective-backed variational server rule as separate claim owners, with no robustness guarantee transferred between them. The study suite then exercises the framework as an end-to-end research system: recovery checks anchor the standard-Bayes limit, belief-sharing studies verify the communication baseline, contamination experiments test robust consensus, and extension studies probe moving agents, hierarchical latent structure, sensitivity to acuity and colony size, parameter recovery, and single-host socket-backed federation traces. All reported quantities are generated from deterministic analysis artifacts and injected into the manuscript by token, so the paper, figures, release package, and validation reports remain tied to the same execution record. The open-source repository is ActiveInferenceInstitute/Active_Fedference. This final-release manuscript uses assigned version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22149133; the bound deposited PDF and repository release are controlled by separate publication gates.
items.title: Robust Belief Sharing in Federated Active Inference: A Recovery-Tested Generalized-Variational Framework for Categorical Contamination-Aware Consensus
